recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-20578 unless a future OO decision changes how multiple Device.type concepts should be represented.
issue_request: FHIR-20578 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification OO request for R5 to change Device.type from 0..1 to 0..* so a device instance can carry multiple distinct, non-synonymous type concepts, with definition text saying those repeated types apply to the specific instance.
initial_application: Commit a7f2575daae7bbacd9a22ea439c7ec35a4784f96, merged by f2409b3c69e13268c406a168498173bcd4677190, lists FHIR-20578 in preapplied Device updates and changes the Device.type spreadsheet row from 0..1 to 0..* while adding the specific-instance definition. Commit 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157 preserved those semantics in the current StructureDefinition source format.
additional_context: Device is active in source/fhir.ini. FHIR-20579 is the duplicate parallel DeviceDefinition.type request and points to FHIR-27798 for the DeviceDefinition-side resolution; FHIR-27798 already has a separate no-change audit commit on the combined branch. Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community evidence for FHIR-20578, Device type, or GUDID.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because source/device/structuredefinition-Device.xml already has Device.type max * and the accepted definition that a device instance may have more than one type when those types apply to that specific instance.
